field_notes.attack_power / guarded_damage_negation /: Base values at +0 (Standard affinity) from the page infobox. Scaling grades: S > A > B > C > D > E, null = no scaling.
field_notes.skill.fp_cost: Wiki notation 'X (Y Z)': X = FP cost of the skill itself, Y/Z = FP cost of the light/heavy follow-ups. '-' = none.
field_notes.skill.type: 'Unique Skill' = exclusive skill (never sold as an Ash of War); 'Ash of War skill' = an 'Ash of War: <name>' item exists on the wiki; 'Standard skill (no Ash of War item)' = non-unique skill with no Ash of War item.
field_notes.passive_effects / status_buildup: Innate on-hit effects at +0 (status buildup values grow with upgrades for some weapons).
field_notes.upgrade.material: Smithing Stones => max +25; Somber Smithing Stones => max +10 and the weapon cannot take Ashes of War. null = the wiki page does not document it.
field_notes.upgrade.*_info_source: Where the value comes from: 'wiki (...)' = stated on the weapon page (template, text or upgrade table); 'deduced (...)' / 'game rule (...)' = strict logical consequence of what the page states.
field_notes.upgrade.estimate_if_undocumented: Only present when the wiki page does not document the upgrade path AND the documented examples of the same group (unique skill / other skill / catalyst) support at least medium confidence: statistical guess with its basis. Treat as unverified.
field_notes.upgrade.ash_of_war_changeable / affinity: true/false only when stated by the wiki (or implied by somber material); null = not documented.
field_notes.upgrade.tables: Per-affinity reinforcement data when the page provides it (levels '+N'; 'growth_per_level' = % growth per level as shown on the wiki). Scaling values: grade + coefficient when available. Coverage varies between pages.
field_notes.upgrade.tables_consistent_with_infobox: false = the page's upgrade table +0 physical attack differs from the infobox (wiki data inconsistency, prefer the infobox).
field_notes.regions_mentioned: Map regions detected in the acquisition text (helper for game-progression analysis).
field_notes.acquisition_flags: Heuristic tags derived from the acquisition text.
field_notes.notes / acquisition.details: Bullet text from the wiki; nested bullets are prefixed with '→' (one per nesting level).
field_notes.description / skill.description: English in-game descriptions (weapon page / skill page).
field_notes.skill.stamina_cost_wiki: Same 'X (Y Z)' notation as fp_cost, from the skill page.
field_notes.upgrade.buffable: Only present when the wiki states whether the weapon can be buffed (grease/spells).
field_notes.patch_notes: Balance changes listed on the weapon page: game version, official patch note, community explanation.
field_notes.compatible_ashes_of_war: Only on the few pages that list them.
field_notes.range: Bow/crossbow/ballista range as shown in the infobox (in-game 'Range' value).
field_notes.sorcery_scaling / incantation_scaling: Catalysts: base spell power at +0 from the infobox (Sorcery Scaling for staves, Incantation Scaling for seals).
field_notes.upgrade.tables.*.spell_buff: Catalysts: sorcery/incantation scaling at that upgrade level ('?' on the wiki => omitted).

entries.name: Dagger

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

entries.description:
A standard dagger with a straight blade.

Though modest in reach and capacity for harm, this weapon is light enough to jab in rapid succession and delivers devastating critical hits.

details: 1 sold by the Twin Maiden Husks at Roundtable Hold for 400 Runes.

A base 4% chance to drop from drop dagger-wielding enemies (Highwaymen, Godrick Foot Soldiers, Raya Lucaria Foot Soldiers, Radahn Foot Soldiers, Leyndell Foot Soldiers, Haligtree Foot Soldiers, and Messmer Foot Soldiers).
→ A good early farming spot is all the Highwaymen at the beginning of Murkwater Cave.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Together with the Rapier this weapon has the second strongest critical multiplier at 130 (the Miséricorde has the highest, at 140).

Has low enough requirements to be used with any starting class's default attributes and is fairly common, making it a decent secondary weapon for backstabbing and other critical hits, especially for those who don't have the stats to wield the Miséricorde.

Generally Dexterity-leaning on its affinities and performs best on a Keen affinity (having scaling just short of S-tier scaling) but also works surprisingly well with the Occult affinity, even if it lacks any of the innate Status Effects required to truly take advantage of this.

→ Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
The shortest of all daggers.

entries.name: Fire Knight's Shortsword
entries.japanese_name: 火の騎士の短剣 (Hi no Kishi no Tanken)

skill.name: Quickstep
skill.description:
Skill prized by the crafty and fleet of foot.
Perform a quickstep maneuver that allows for circling around lock-on targets.

entries.description:
Shortsword used by the Fire Knights. A slender blade that undulates like fire.

Blessed with a flame incantation. Further flame imbuement will amplify the effect and greatly increase the armament's power.

details: Dropped by dual dagger-wielding Fire Knights with a 4% droprate.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
Generally leans towards Dexterity-scaling over Strength-scaling.

Despite the description this dagger actually has higher Faith-scaling and raw Attack Power (AP) on a Sacred affinity than on a Flame Art affinity. It's also outclassed in raw AP by a Flame Art affinity Erdsteel Dagger.

→ However, the Fire Knight's Shortsword's Flame Art affinity usually has higher effective damage than the Sacred affinity due to only having to bypass 2 flat defences rather than 3, and the Fire damage will be higher on its own than either the Sacred affinity's Holy damage or the Flame Art Erdsteel Dagger's Fire damage.
Surprisingly enough, since this weapon is themed after Faith and Fire, it actually has the strongest Intelligence-scaling of all Daggers on the Magic and Cold affinities.
Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger.
→ This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2, due to hitting twice.

Though the innate Fire damage is low on all but the Fire and Flame Art affinities, simply having it means it will immediate reset fully applied Frostbite on the next hit if using Frostbite-causing skills such as Chilling Mist. It will also stun enemies that are extremely vulnerable to fire, such as Fingercreepers and Miranda Sprouts and Blossoms.

→ There is a bug, where using the Magic, Cold, Lightning, or Sacred Affinities with this weapon prevents the usual on-hit effect from dealing Fire damage from taking place. This means that using any of those Affinities means that the weapon won't stun Fingercreepers, won't detonate red barrels, and won't remove fully applied Frostbite from targets.
→→ This also applies to the Fire Knight's Greatsword and Queelign's Greatsword.
If choosing any of the Magic, Cold, Blood, Poison, or Occult affinities this is one of the few weapons that can scale with four separate stats.

→ In the base game the ability to scale with four different stats via affinities was only held by the Clayman's Harpoon and the Erdsteel Dagger, while the DLC added the Black Steel Greathammer, Bloodfiend's Arm, and Fire Knight's Greatsword, weapons which all have the same quality.

entries.name: Scorpion's Stinger

skill.name: Repeating Thrust
skill.description: Twist to build power, then unleash a flurry of thrusts.

entries.description:
Dagger fashioned from a great scorpion's tail, glistening with scarlet rot.

A ceremonial tool used by heretics, crafted from the relic of a sealed outer god.

details: Found inside a chest near the Grand Cloister Site of Grace, located in the Lake of Rot. It inside the small shrine to the west that is guarded by a large group of Kindred of Rot.

notes: The Scorpion's Stinger cannot be buffed by spells or any consumables.
The Scorpion's Stinger cannot have its Skill or Affinity changed.
The locked skill, Repeating Thrust, is somewhat useful for applying the weapon's innate Scarlet Rot though does notably lack the extra mobility from the usual Quickstep skill.
Scales quite well with Dexterity, enough to be neck-and-neck with the Parrying Dagger and the Celebrant's Sickle and to only be substantially surpassed by the Wakizashi.
Has a unique, thrusting heavy attack compared to the standard daggers moveset. This trait is shared with the Glintstone Kris, Main-gauche, and the Miséricorde.
The Scarlet Rot build-up is flat; it does not increase no matter the stat investment or weapon upgrade level.

entries.name: Smithscript Dagger

skill.name: Piercing Throw
skill.description: Throw armament with a powerful spin, causing it to bore through foes. When using this skill, the armament can be thrown further than normal and also pierce through enemies

entries.description:
Dagger engraved with a smithscript.

Reduced mass enhances the effects of the smithing arts, allowing this weapon to function as a throwing dagger for all attacks.

Once thrown, the dagger instantly reappears in the wielder's hand.

details: Proceed normally through the dungeon until you reach the lever that moves the lava pipe and then drop down to the floor below. The dagger can be found on a body behind a Golem Smith.

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 75 of 92 wiki-documented weapons with a non-unique skill use regular Smithing Stones

notes: Though subpar as a standalone weapon due to low damage and Status Effect build-up, the Smithscript Dagger is an excellent offhand weapon due to its very low weight, quick attacks, and decent range that lets it inflict small amounts of chip damage on opponents and potentially keep Status Effect build-up and Stance damage from decaying.

→ The available Ashes of War are better of selected from with the same criteria, with more utiliy-based skills such as Endure, Kick, Parry, or Quickstep fitting better than anything dependent on the weapon's Attack Power.
Every attack except for its Critical Attacks are throwing attacks, meaning this weapon benefits alot from the Smithing Talisman +10% damage boost.
→ The thrown attacks also partially benefit from the Arrow's Reach Talisman as while their range isn't increased the damage falloff experienced at longer ranges is decreased.

All different light attacks have an extremely low Damage Level value of 0 (No Stagger) and therefore are extremely bad at interrupting opponents, with one of the most notable conseqeuences being that it cannot break the bubbles that protect the Juvenile Scholars during Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon's first phase instead just killing them.

→ All different heavy attacks do at the very least a Damage Level value of 1 (Short Stagger), or 2 (Moderate Stagger) for the charged heavy attacks, meaning it is at least possible to interrupt these things with the correct attacks.
→ Note that this is not the same as dealing no Poise or Stance damage, even if the Weapon Class has the lowest possible base value of 2 for both of these.

patch_notes.community_notes:
This is referring to the raw attack power of the critical hit and not the modifier; the critical hit modifier is still 100.
More specifically the innate multiplier for these attacks increased by 15-40% (from 220% to 280% for backstabs, from 300% to 420% for ripostes, from 420% to 483% for small PvE foes, and from 280% to?% for ripostes against large PvE foes).

patch_notes.official_notes: Extended the Smithscript Dagger’s throwing attacks range.
patch_notes.community_notes: With this update the non-skill attacks have a range roughly four times the original range.

patch_notes.official_notes: Extended the throwing attacks range for the following weapons: Smithscript Dagger / Smithscript Cirque.
patch_notes.community_notes:
Prior to this update the range of the non-skill attacks was extremely short, roughly 2 character lengths.
After the update the range is slightly longer, roughly 3 character lengths.

entries.name: Longsword

skill.name: Square Off
skill.description: This skill starts with the sword held level. Follow up with a normal attack to slash upwards through enemy's guard, or a strong attack to perform a running thrust.
skill.attack_type: Weapon's Primary Damage type/Weapon's Secondary Damage type

entries.description:
A straight sword with a double-edged blade.

In addition to its reliable standard damage, this weapon also boasts powerful piercing attacks. A superbly balanced armament.

details: Starting armament of the Vagabond origin.
Purchased from Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold for 1,000 Runes.

notes: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
The default skill is useful for breaking the guard of blocking enemies with the light attack version or for breaking their Stance with the heavy attack version.
Consistently the second strongest of all regular Straight Swords, outmatched only by the Broadsword, almost matching it on a Keen affinity and outclassing it on a Quality affinity.
→ This may be somewhat surprising since the Longsword's scaling values leans towards Strength more so than Dexterity, but it's primarily because the Broadsword scales rather less well on Keen.
→ Quality affinity requires high stats to use properly, making this somewhat difficult to exploit before New Game Plus/Journey 2 and later.

While not quite to the level of the Short Sword's unique heavy attack chain, since the first heavy attack in a chain is a Pierce damage attack as well as the heavy variant of its default skill and as such can hit for heavy counter damage with the Spear Talisman.

entries.name: Idus Sword

skill.name: Impaling Thrust
skill.description: Skill that lets piercing armaments overcome enemy shields. Build power, then lunge forward for a strong thrust that pierces an enemy's guard.
skill.stamina_cost_wiki: 40 (39 for CSS Shadow of the Erdtree) (- -)

entries.description:
A light greatsword; that is, a sword whose blade matches the length of a greatsword, while only possessing a very light weight due to its remarkable manufacture.

A signature weapon in the land of Idus.

With cultivated form, one can wield this weapon as swiftly as one might a straight sword.

details: The Idus Sword is the starting weapon for the Idus Knight.

acquisition.location: Liurnia of the Lakes Tarnished Pack
details: Found early into the Laskyar Ruins past the Nomadic Merchant in the Liurnia Lake Shore Site of Grace. Northwest of the merchant, following the rock wall which seats the Malefactor's Evergaol, there will be a tree with two Revenant Followers. Slaying them is ideal, since they will use their bells to summon ranged projectiles, but it can be obtained without doing so.
The path to the Idus Sword.

upgrade.material_info_source: deduced (wiki shows the weapon accepts Ashes of War/affinities; somber weapons cannot)

notes: Though the Idus Sword sports higher base damage than the other infusable Light Greatsword, the Milady, it has worse scaling. This means that as the Tarnished increases their levels of Dexterity (or Strength, Intelligence, etc.) they will not receive as much of a damage benefit from weapon scaling as they progress. However, the true strength of the Idus Sword is its accessiblity: depending on what class one chooses, it can be wielded either very early on or at the very beginning of the game.
As an infusable Light Greatsword, this is one of only two weapons able to take advantage of the synergy with Status Effect-based Affinities and the multi-hit attacks in the Light Greatsword moveset.
→ This applies more specifically to the one- and two-handed heavy attacks, charged heavy attacks, running heavy attacks, and jumping heavy attacks.

entries.name: Leda's Sword

skill.name: Needle Piercer
skill.description: Skill of Needle Knight Leda. Generates ten gold needles which pierce their target all at once. Those pierced are purged of all ailments and special effects alike.

entries.description:
Light greatsword with gold inlaid. Weapon of Leda, the Needle Knight. Deals holy damage.

Though polished to a mirror sheen, this blade still reeks with the stench of crusted blood that lingers from the cull of her knightly comrades.

details: Received after defeating Leda and her allies in their boss fight near the top of Enir-Ilim.

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: Hitting a foe with the innate skill, Needle Piercer, will purge them of any active Status Effects and Buffs.

While the weapon scales with several stats, it's only really Dexterity that is useful for increasing its Attack Power due to the other two stats having much weaker scalings (Strength and Faith) and working off the weaker Holy Attack Power instead of the stronger Physical Attack Power (Faith only).

upgrade.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

entries.name: Blasphemous Blade

skill.name: Taker's Flames
skill.description: Raise the sacred sword aloft to set it ablaze with blasphemous flames, then bring it down to fire off a forward blast. The flames steal HP from those they touch.

passive_effects: Restores HP equal to 4% of maximum HP + 40 upon nearby deaths
entries.description:
Sacred sword of Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy. Remains of the countless heroes he has devoured writhe upon the surface of this blade.

Now they share the same blood, bound together as family. Some HP is restored upon defeating an enemy.

details: Trade the Remembrance of the Blasphemous, gained by defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, with Finger Reader Enia.
→ Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums with a bell to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: Note that the innate skill Taker's Flames, unlike the weapon, only scales with Faith through the Fire Attack Power of the weapon.
→ The skill also serves as the weapon's strongest attack, with roughly twice as much Attack Power as the weapon itself.
Restores HP equal to (4% of wielder's maximum HP + 40) if a nearby creature is killed while the sword is held in an active hand.
→ Effect stacks with Greathorn Hammer, Serpent-God's Curved Sword and Taker's Cameo.
→ This is in addition to the skill restoring HP equal to (10% of target's maximum HP + 150) upon hit.
Very heavy for a greatsword, being outweighed only by the Greatsword of Solitude.

Though the Faith-scaling is technically stronger than both its Strength- and Dexterity-scalings, as it scales with the lower Fire Attack Power instead of the higher Physical Attack Power it's effectively a very high D-scaling that is just ever so slightly lower than the other stats' very low C-scaling.

→ Overall, a hybrid Strength-Dexterity or Dexterity-Faith build gains the most Attack Power, while a pure Faith build sacrifices about 6% more weapon Attack Power in exchange for 12% more skill Attack Power.

entries.name: Moonveil

skill.name: Transient Moonlight
skill.description: Sheathe blade, holding it at the hip in a composed stance. Follow up with either a normal or a strong attack to draw the blade at great speed for an instant slash attack. Both attacks fire off a wave of light.

entries.description:
Katana forged of glintstone. Masterpiece of a Sellian swordsmith.

Light enwreathes the blade when sheathed, explaining its Moonveil moniker.

details: Dropped by the Magma Wyrm in Gael Tunnel.

estimate_if_undocumented.basis: 57 of 58 wiki-documented weapons with a Unique Skill use Somber Smithing Stones

notes: The Unique Skill: Transient Moonlight is the regular Skill: Unsheathe but with added projectiles: a short-ranged one for the light attack sweep and a mid-ranged one for the heavy attack overhead slash.

→ The skill is useful in roughly the same ways that Unsheathe is, meaning that the light attack follow-up is generally slightly quicker and much wider in exchange for being slightly weaker, while the heavy attack follow-up hits a single target slightly harder and is slightly more difficult to roll directly away from.

→→ One stark difference is that the different attacks are much less dissimilar, with the light attack follow-up having less of a damage difference (22% less for Unsheathe, 10% less for Transient Moonlight) and much less of a Stance damage difference (50% less for Unsheathe, 8% less for Transient Moonlight).

→ While this does give the weapon some more reach (though mostly with the heavy attack follow-up), the skill is still the most effective at melee range since that means both the weapon and the magic waves can hit the target.
→ The skill's heavy attack follow-up has a weird interaction with jumping players and deals a lot less damage against them for some reason.

While a hybrid Intelligence/Dexterity build gains the highest total Attack Power a pure Intelligence build only loses about 2% total Attack Power in exchange for the skill's projectiles getting 13% higher Attack Power, making the latter generally preferable.

A simple, primitive weapon that requires only brute strength and persistence to hammer your foe into the ground.
